decisions.reason: The particle therapy water phantom serves a niche, regulation-heavy market whose uptake is still uncertain, and it was downgraded to a mention in 2019, but it carries strategic option value in proton therapy QA and costs little to keep listed, so the firm holds it.
Small-volume chambers are core dosimetry consumables, cheap to keep in a catalog, and still had their own page in 2019, so there is no evidence the option has resolved negatively.
This second small-volume chamber overlaps somewhat with B, which raises consolidation risk, but carrying costs are low and demand for small-field dosimetry keeps growing, so it stays.
A standard clinical ionization chamber is a staple product with steady recalibration-driven demand and little carrying cost, so dropping it makes no sense.
A relative dosimetry chamber complements the firm's water phantom systems and its platform strategy, and it was still featured on its own page, so the firm keeps it.
A thimble chamber is a low-cost, established product type within the firm's dosimetry core, so keeping it is worth more than the resources dropping it would free.
